item.title: protect_items_from_groom and enforce_groom_limits write directly to live backlog — no atomic swap
item.intent: All backlog file writes in groom protection and limit enforcement must be atomic; direct truncating writes must be replaced with temp-file-then-mv
steps: Locate direct write in protect_items_from_groom: sed '$d' <<< "$output" > "$live_file" (line ~3172)
Locate direct write in enforce_groom_limits: printf '%s\n' "$tmp" > "$live_file" (line ~3238)
Compare with update_item which correctly uses: jq ... > tmpfile && mv tmpfile live_file
Fix protect_items_from_groom: write to a temp file via ensure_tmpdir, then mv atomically to live_file; ensure sed failure leaves live_file intact
Fix enforce_groom_limits: same pattern — write jq output to temp file, mv to live_file; ensure jq failure leaves live_file intact
Run shellcheck — confirm zero new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: If jq or sed returns non-zero in either function, the live backlog file is unchanged (not truncated or partially written)
Normal groom flow still completes successfully: items are protected and limits enforced correctly
